title: Evaluation of a supportive group intervention for families with a parent suffering from cancer
summary:
When a parent in a family develops cancer, all family members are affected. In addition to the emotional strain, family routines and everyday life are disrupted. That is why we now speak of “we disease” when it comes to cancer, and in addition to the patients, their partners and children are often highly stressed. While there are support services for individual family members, there are hardly any interventions that focus on the family as a whole. 
Therefore, in 2024, the “Auszeit für Familien” was developed by the psycho-oncology team at the NCT. The intervention is aimed at families with a parent suffering from cancer, regardless of the type of tumor and the disease situation (curative/palliative). The “time out for families” includes 2 days (including overnight accommodation) and is intended as an opportunity to leave the stressful everyday life behind and to recharge as a family. In addition to resource-oriented offers, the focus is on exchange and community with families in a similar life situation. This is realized through various activities for the whole family, in which they should experience themselves as a “family team”, as well as through age-specific workshops for children, adolescents and parents.
This intervention is accompanied by a qualitative evaluation in the form of questionnaires and focus groups to capture how all participants experienced the family time out. This qualitative evaluation is intended to optimize the intervention so that it can be integrated into the psycho-oncological care program in the long term.
conditions: Patients with cancer and their families

interventions.name: Participation in a two-day resource-oriented family therapy intervention. This is followed by completion of a qualitative questionnaire and participation in a focus group discussion.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patients with an oncological disease and their family, regardless of the type and stage of the tumor disease, 
ability to consent to study participation
Exclusion criteria:
The main exclusion criterion is the lack of a signed declaration of consent. Another exclusion criterion is the occurrence of severe mental disorders within the last two years, i.e. psychotic disorders, bipolar disorders, severe depression and acute suicidality.
